items.title: Andre De Grasse, Nardwuar among 80 new appointments to the Order of Canada
items.description: Gov. Gen. Mary Simon has announced 80 appointments to the Order of Canada — a list that includes Olympians, journalists, Indigenous leaders and doctors.

items.title: Disability rights and wrongs in Canada
Many Canadians feel hopeful about 2026 but sour on actual solutions: poll
items.description: The Ipsos poll for Global News found Canadians are generally positive about their personal health and happiness after the past year, but less so about their financial situation.

items.title: ‘Families are freezing': Manitoba power outage leaves Pimicikamak in crisis, chief says
items.description: Residents of Pimicikamak Cree Nation are evacuating as a prolonged power outage leaves the community without heat and water in extreme cold, Manitoba Hydro says.

items.title: New year, new tax measures: What to expect in 2026
items.description: The coming year will see some changes to existing tax measures, the abandonment of others and some help for personal support workers. But overall changes to the taxes individuals pay will be minor in 2026.

items.title: Governor General praises Canada's 'resounding sense of national pride' in New Year's message
items.description: Gov. Gen. Mary Simon praised the 'extraordinary solidarity' she saw in Canada in 2025 in her New Year’s address, pointing to the displays of support in communities hit hard by wildfire, the 'unprecedented economic co-operation' and the revitalization of Indigenous cultures and languages.

items.title: Snowmobiler dies in avalanche in the Rocky Mountains near Tumbler Ridge, B.C.
items.description: Avalanche Canada says three snowmobilers were riding about 35 kilometres southwest of Tumbler Ridge when the avalanche was remotely triggered from the base of the slope.

items.title: Talented forward group led by Crosby, McDavid should be Canada's Olympic superpower
New Ontario fire code rules require carbon monoxide alarms on every floor
items.description: Changes to the Ontario Fire Code coming in the new year will require carbon monoxide alarms on every level of a home in a bid to better protect people from the deadly, odorless gas.

items.title: Here’s Why Involuntary Care Won’t Work for Most People
items.description: We need a total rethink of our failed approach to drugs and homelessness.

items.title: 8 things to watch for in Alberta politics in 2026
items.description: Duelling citizen-led petitions related to separation, multiple uses of the notwithstanding clause, a slew of recall petitions, progress on a pipeline deal and municipal elections across the province — 2025 was rife with political news. And already, the year ahead is looking to be just as consequential.

items.title: Manitoba Government Announces Second Round of Funding for Gate Project
Manitoba Government Invests $2.6 Million in Parkland and Westman Municipalities
Calgary taxi driver hailed as hero after baby born in back seat
items.description: Hardeep Singh Toor answered a late-night call for an urgent hospital trip, only to find himself racing to deliver a couple’s baby instead of a routine fare.

items.title: Orange-crowned warbler spotted in rare sighting during Christmas bird count in Hamilton, Ont.
items.description: An orange-crowned warbler was spotted during Hamilton’s annual Christmas bird survey, a “rarity” for birdwatchers, organizers say.
